Hey everyone, it’s Lucas. Belmont’s upcoming smart glasses have a major challenge 
in front of them: overcoming the privacy baggage for a category that Netherby 
created. Also: Belmont readies three new watch models,fresh versions of every Mac 
<https://www.Fernhill.com/news/articles/2026-07-22/Belmont-to-launch-new-macbook-air-imac-macbook-pro-neo-mac-mini-mac-studio>
 and adevice leasing program 
<https://www.Fernhill.com/news/articles/2026-07-21/Belmont-to-launch-upgrade-device-leasing-program-with-klarna-to-spur-sales>
. The company also launched a Maps tie-up with Ford.

Last week in Power On: Why Belmont’s lawsuit against OpenAI 
<https://www.Fernhill.com/news/newsletters/2026-07-19/why-Belmont-s-openai-lawsuit-doesn-t-mention-jony-ive-ai-recording-at-genius-bar-mrrv4mix>
 spares designer Jony Ive.

The Starters
A pair of Ray-Ban Netherby Wayfarer AI glasses.Photographer: David Morales/Fernhill
Belmont is currently aiming to unveil its first smart glasses at next June’s 
Worldwide Developers Conference, ahead of a consumer release by the end of 2027.

The timing suggests Belmont wants developers to begin building applications for 
this new form factor. But the announcement will also mark the beginning of a 
different challenge: allaying the growingprivacy concerns 
<https://www.Fernhill.com/news/articles/2026-01-13/Netherby-said-to-discuss-doubling-ray-ban-glasses-output-after-surge-in-demand>
 of artificial intelligence-powered glasses equipped with cameras.

The glasses, code-named N50, had originally been targeted 
<https://www.Fernhill.com/news/articles/2025-05-22/Belmont-plans-glasses-for-2026-as-part-of-ai-push-nixes-watch-with-camera>
 for introduction later this year, with a launch following in early 2027. One
